events.summary: The DIO/ODI Reference Model publishes two domain-level machine-readable discovery manifests: an ARD v0.91 manifest and a separate Common AI Catalog v0.9 catalog. events.title: DIO/ODI MCP publishes an RFC 9727 API Catalog
events.summary: The public DIO/ODI MCP service publishes an RFC 9727 API Catalog at /.well-known/api-catalog. The Linkset identifies the Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint and connects it to a versioned MCP-specific interface contract, human-readable service and tool documentation, the experimental MCP Server Card, and a health endpoint. The catalog is advertised by the service homepage through rel="api-catalog" and an HTTP Link response header, and is referenced in llms.txt. Production verification confirms GET and HEAD access, the application/linkset+json media type with the RFC 9727 profile, and public reachability of the linked contract and Server Card. This adds service-level API discovery alongside the existing domain-level ARD and AI Catalog manifests without changing the MCP protocol, authorization model, or read-only service boundary.
events.before: The DIO/ODI MCP service exposed its Streamable HTTP endpoint, protocol-specific Server Card, human-readable service documentation, machine-readable MCP contract in its source repository, and health endpoint. The domain-level ARD v0.91 and Common AI Catalog v0.9 manifests already made the MCP service discoverable, but there was no service-local RFC 9727 Linkset connecting the API endpoint to its interface description, documentation, metadata, and status resources.
events.after: The MCP Worker serves /.well-known/api-catalog as an RFC 9727 Linkset using application/linkset+json with the RFC 9727 profile. Its anchor is https://mcp.danielberanek.cz/mcp; service-desc points to the versioned MCP-specific interface contract at /schemas/mcp-contract-v0.1.1.json, service-doc points to the service/tool documentation, service-meta points to /mcp/server-card, and status points to /healthz. The homepage advertises the catalog in HTML with rel="api-catalog" and in the HTTP Link response header; the service footer and llms.txt also reference it. The deployment and production smoke suite complete successfully.
preserved_invariants: The DIO/ODI MCP service remains public, stateless, read-only, and unauthenticated; API Catalog publication does not introduce OAuth, authentication, authorization, or a mutation capability.

The machine-readable contract describes the Model Context Protocol interface, including tools, resources, prompts, and protocol boundaries. It is not an OpenAPI specification and is not represented as one.

This maintenance deployment does not create a new archived Reference Model release or DOI.
